"Open source software is often described as free, but the word 'free' misleads. What is free is not necessarily the price; it is the liberty to read the source code, modify it and share the modified version. Many governments have adopted such software for exactly this reason. When the code of a system that stores citizens' data can be inspected by independent experts, hidden flaws are found sooner. Cost savings, where they occur, are a secondary benefit. Critics point out that adoption requires trained staff and a support ecosystem, without which an organisation may find itself holding software that nobody can maintain. That objection is fair, and it explains why the most successful migrations have been gradual rather than sudden."

In the context of open source, the word 'free' primarily refers to —
options: the liberty to read, modify and share the code
explanation: "What is free is not necessarily the price; it is the liberty to read the source code, modify it and share…"। लेखक स्पष्ट रूप से क़ीमत वाले अर्थ को नकार रहा है।
